story_type: first flight of a new crewed spacecraft
hook: Two men rode a spaceship that had never been to space.
narration: Two men rode a spaceship that had never once been to space.
April twelfth, nineteen eighty one. Space Shuttle Columbia stood on the pad in Florida.
Commander John Young and pilot Robert Crippen climbed aboard.
It was a test mission, the first time a shuttle had ever flown to space.
The three main engines lit first, then the two solid rocket boosters, which cannot be shut off once they light.
Columbia cleared the tower and climbed toward orbit.
It circled Earth thirty seven times in fifty four and a half hours.
[short pause] Inside, the two pilots tested every system, and floated.
outcome: With no engines running, Columbia glided to a landing at Edwards Air Force Base in California.
title: Shuttle Columbia's first ride to space
description:
Space Shuttle Columbia lifted off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center on STS-1, the first flight of the Space Shuttle Program, on April 12, 1981, with John Young and Robert Crippen aboard, and landed at Edwards Air Force Base two days later.

facts.claim: STS-1 lifted off April 12, 1981 with Young and Crippen aboard
facts.source_quote: The Space Shuttle Columbia began a new era of manned spaceflight when it lifted off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center on STS-1, the inaugural flight in the Space Shuttle Program on April 12, 1981. Aboard the spacecraft were astronauts John W. Young, commander, and Robert L. Crippen, pilot.

facts.claim: Test mission, first time a shuttle flew to space
facts.source_quote: The flight was a test mission and the first time a shuttle was flown to space.
During the mission, Columbia orbited Earth 37 times in 54.5 hours.

facts.claim: Landing at Edwards Air Force Base
facts.source_quote: Columbia glided to a landing at Edwards Air Force Base in California on April 14, 1981, completing its historic mission.
And the shuttle has cleared the tower.
